name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA is a large scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content. Questions are categorized based on their reasoning requirements (9 question types). The dataset covers a multitude of different document types including tables, forms, figures, and a range of textual, graphical and structural elements. Documents span many decades and originate from 5 different industries.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality as a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage annotation process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/). The final set of images is drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018, from 5 major industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: OCR tokens from document images were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order. For BERT QA models, answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string, following an approach proposed in TriviaQA.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized in the dataset. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity during stage 2 annotation were excluded from the dataset. Questions where answers from stage 1 and stage 2 did not match were sent for a third-stage review. The data is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted, and instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. Stage 2: A different worker was shown the image and questions from stage 1 (without stage 1 answers) and required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting or ignoring them.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Web-based annotation tool (custom, screen grabs shown in appendix)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in stage 1 match exactly with any of the answers from stage 2, the question is sent for third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt in stage 2 are not included in the dataset. The ANLS metric is used as the primary evaluation metric to account for minor answer mismatches stemming from OCR errors.
rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image; multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted. Each question was answered independently in stage 2 and assigned one or more question types.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers (crowd workers) for stages 1 and 2; authors of the paper for stage 3 review. A few volunteers from the authors' institution were used for measuring human performance on the test split.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application (used to extract OCR tokens from document images for baselines and upper bound computation)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains industry documents that may include names of people, institutions, and places as part of the document content. Named entities such as names of people appear among the most frequent answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research, driving methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance. It seeks to enable intelligent reading systems that can respond to ad-hoc requests for information expressed in natural language.
rai:dataBiases: A large majority of questions start with 'what is the', asking for date, title, total, amount or name. Almost all of the top answers are numeric values, which is expected since there are a good number of document images of reports and invoices. Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections as they have a good number of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the UCSF library are binarized, which takes a toll on image quality; binarized images were minimized but not entirely excluded. OCR errors can result in incorrect model answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models struggle with questions requiring understanding of figures, diagrams, photographs, and handwritten text. The dataset is limited to English-language industry documents from 5 industries.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. The dataset is split 80-10-10 for train, validation, and test. It can be used to benchmark reading comprehension models and scene text VQA models on document images. A leaderboard is available at docvqa.org.
